item.title: 雅思口语Part 1高分语料 | Swimming 你喜欢游泳吗？
item.description:
你好呀，欢迎收听：英语考试Cat 🐱🐱🐱🐱

How often do you go swimming?

Well, never actually because I haven't learnt. That said, I love being around water, whether I'm at the beach or beside a swimming pool. In those moments, I really wish I could swim.

When did you learn how to swim?

As said, I've honestly never learnt to swim. I have quite a strong fear of water, which you could call aquaphobia. When I was little, I nearly drowned in a reservoir near where I grew up. That incident left me with a lasting fear of water, so I've never plucked up the courage to take swimming lessons.

Will you swim a lot in the future?

I really hope so. Swimming is definitely a skill I'm keen to pick up someday. Once I’m confident in the water, I'd love to swim in all sorts of places — a swimming pool, a lake, or even the ocean.

Can most people in your country swim?

I think it really depends on where people live. Those who grow up in coastal areas or beside rivers or other bodies of water tend to learn swimming from an early age. By contrast, people living in mountainous regions are far less likely to be able to swim. Even so, plenty of parents now sign their children up for weekend swimming classes, and lots of urban residents, especially in tier one cities, treat swimming in pools as a regular summer activity and an important skill.

  • aquaphobia /ˌækwəˈfəʊbiə/ 恐水症

  • drowned /draʊnd/ 溺水

  • left me with a lasting fear of 给我留下长久的…… 恐惧

  • plucked up the courage to 鼓起勇气去

  • keen to pick up 很想学会

  • all sorts of places 各种各样的地方

  • bodies of water 水域

  • from an early age 从小

  • mountainous regions 山区

  • far less likely to 不太可能……

  • sign their children up 给孩子报名

  • urban residents 城市居民

  • tier one cities 一线城市

item.title: 雅思口语Part 1高分语料 | Sport teams 团体运动
item.description:
你好呀，欢迎收听：英语考试Cat 🐱🐱🐱🐱

Have you ever been part of a sport team?

No, never. I'm really not into sports at all. In fact, I can't remember joining any sport teams growing up. I'm just terrible at pretty much every sport. For example, my friends would get so frustrated playing badminton with me because I could barely hit the birdie. It just wasn't an enjoyable experience for them or for myself.

 - I'm really not into 我不太喜欢

- growing up 从小到大

- terrible at 不擅长

- frustrated 沮丧、泄气

- the birdie 羽毛球

- an enjoyable experience 一段愉快的经历

Are team sports popular in your culture?

Not really, though over the last decade or so they have become more popular. However, in saying that, sports like basketball and football have a significant following. And I would say that for basketball, probably the majority of teenagers and young adults have played at one time or another.  Solo sporting activities, such as ping-pong, badminton, and even tennis tend to be more popular as far as people playing them. Lots of people also prefer casual solo activities like jogging or hiking instead.

 - have become 已经变得

- a significant following 一大批爱好者、不少追随者

- the majority of 大多数

- Solo sporting activities 单人运动项目

- casual 休闲的

- jogging 慢跑

- hiking 徒步、远足

Do you like to watch team games? Why?

To be honest, not at all unless watching them live. Watching sports on TV, especially team sports, for me is really boring, but in a stadium is a different, forgive the pun, ball game. Though I might not fully understand all the rules and details of the sport, I adore soaking up the electric atmosphere of a live game. Earlier this month, for instance, I went to a college football match in an 80,000-capacity stadium, and it was incredible. Everyone was shouting at the top of their lungs, cheering for their team. It was like an extravaganza, so that made the whole event electrifying and exciting.

 - watching them live 现场观看（比赛）

- a stadium 体育场

- forgive the pun 恕我玩个文字梗（pun 双关语）

- not fully understand 不完全理解

- soaking up the electric atmosphere 感受热烈激动的氛围

- football match 橄榄球赛

- 80,000-capacity stadium 可容纳 8 万人的体育场

- shouting at the top of their lungs 扯着嗓子呼喊

- cheering for their team 为他们支持的队伍加油

- an extravaganza 盛大精彩的活动

What are the differences between team sports and individual sports?

Team sports centre on collaboration. While individual talent matters, how well players cooperate as a group is equally vital. Individual sports are a different story as it all comes down to the player's own skill, stamina and mental strength. There's no teammate to rely on; success or failure falls squarely on the individual.

- centre on 以…… 为核心；围绕

- individual talent 个人天赋

- cooperate as a group 团队协作

- equally vital 同样重要

- a different story 另一回事、情况不一样

- all comes down to 归根结底在于

- mental strength 心理素质

- falls squarely on the individual 成败完全由个人承担

item.title: 雅思口语Part 1高分语料 | Hometown 聊聊你的家乡
item.description:
你好呀，欢迎收听：英语考试Cat 🐱🐱🐱🐱

Where is your hometown?

My hometown is a tiny hamlet nestled in the foothills of northeastern Sichuan. It sits at about 700 metres above sea level, so winters get pretty cold there. Its really in the middle of nowhere, actually. When I was a kid, I used to climb to a higher vantage point near my house and look out, and all you could see was hills, hills and even more hills stretching all the way to the horizon.

  •  hamlet：小村庄、小村落（规模小于普通 village，多指偏僻的小型居民点）

  1. nestled in：坐落于、掩映在

  2. foothills：山脚丘陵带

  3. sits at：位于、坐落在

  4. above sea level：海拔

  5. in the middle of nowhere：偏远之地

  6. a higher vantage point：视野更佳的高处（vantage point 指视野开阔、便于观察的有利位置）

  7. look out：放眼望去

  8. all you could see was：目之所及尽是

  9. stretching all the way to the horizon：一直延伸到天际、绵延至地平线

How long have you lived there?

I lived there for the first 16 years of my life, then I moved away to go to senior high school and university in other cities.

 

Did you like living there?

On the whole, I didn't mind living there at all because the natural scenery is beautiful. Growing up surrounded by nature taught me to appreciate the outdoors and made me pretty tough as a person. Also, life there was and still is really traditional and slow-paced. On market days, you can still pick up fresh vegetables grown by locals and lots of handmade crafts. So yeah, it's a nice place to be.

 didn't mind living there at all：一点也不反感住在那儿

  1. the natural scenery：自然风光

  2. surrounded by nature：被大自然环抱

  3. appreciate the outdoors：喜爱户外自然环境

  4. made me pretty tough：十分坚韧

  5. On market days：赶集的日子

  6. fresh vegetables：新鲜蔬菜

  7. handmade crafts：手工艺品

Do you think you will continue living there for a long time?

No, I don't think so. I left that mountain town when I was 16. After that I only went back during school holidays, and once I started working, I only go back once or twice a year – one of those trips is always for Chinese New Year. In a way, time feels like it stands still there; the way of life is largely unchanged. But I can't see myself going back there for any substantial period of time. There's no real industry there, so decent jobs are really hard to come by. It kind of feels like you can already see exactly what the rest of your life would look like if you stayed, and that’s exactly why I left in the first place.

  1. during school holidays：在寒暑假期间

  2. go back once or twice a year：一年回去一两次

  3. time feels like it stands still：时光仿佛静止了

  4. largely unchanged：基本没什么变化

  5. can't see myself：无法想象自己（做某事）

  6. substantial period of time：很长一段时间

  7. no real industry：没有成型的产业

  8. decent jobs：不错的工作

  9. hard to come by：不容易找到

  10. the rest of your life：你的余生

  11. in the first place：当初

item.title: 雅思口语Part 3高分语料 | Working overseas 海外工作
item.description:
你好呀，欢迎收听：英语考试Cat 🐱🐱🐱🐱

Why do some people not like working in a foreign country?

Well, I guess there are a few obvious reasons. For one thing, there’s the language barrier: even if you speak English, say, operating in a full-time position at work, it's totally different from casual use, and a lot of people find it challenging and exhausting.

Then there's the cultural side of it. All the little workplace norms and unwritten rules you take for granted back home might not work at all, and you're basically back to square one learning how everything works. On top of that, you leave your whole social network behind, and so you have to build new friendships and connections from scratch, and that can take ages. Also, many people will simply become homesick, missing everything from their family to food.

At the end of the day, everything is new, and for people who don't really enjoy throwing themselves into unfamiliar situations, I imagine it could feel like an uphill battle.

  • language barrier 语言障碍

  • exhausting 心力交瘁

  • the cultural side of it 文化层面

  • workplace norms 职场行为准则

  • unwritten rules 不成文的规则

  • take for granted 视为理所当然

  • back home 在国内

  • might not work at all 完全行不通

  • back to square one 回到原点

  • social network 社交圈子

  • from scratch 从零开始

  • take ages 耗费很长时间

  • throwing themselves into unfamiliar situations 投入陌生环境

  • feel like an uphill battle 举步维艰

What important skills do people need when working in companies?

I think there are a few that matter, no matter how big or small the company is. First off, you've got to have actual expertise in what you do – solid knowledge of your field is the baseline, obviously.

Then you need to know how to work with other people, being a team player. Most jobs aren't solo work, so being able to get along with different types of people is a significant factor. Communication skills and time management are a given too, I'd say.

And I'd add one more that I think is really underrated: empathy. A lot of people only focus on hard skills, but being able to understand where your colleagues are coming from makes such a difference to how a team functions long term.

  • expertise in what you do 专业能力

  • solid knowledge of your field 扎实的行业领域知识

  • the baseline 基准

  • know how to work with other people 懂得如何与他人协作

  • solo work 独立工作

  • able to get along with 能够与…… 和睦相处

  • a significant factor 重要因素

  • a given 理所当然的事；既定事实

  • empathy 共情能力；同理心

How can people demonstrate their abilities when working in a foreign country?

I think it's mostly the same as proving yourself in any company, really: you just deliver good work and hit your targets. But in a foreign country, I'd say language and communication skills are probably the number one thing that shows your ability.

You have to be able to get your point across to your team in a way that's clear and easy to follow. If people can’t understand you properly, it doesn't matter how good your actual work is, it creates friction for everyone. Being able to communicate well removes that barrier straight away.

  • deliver good work 交付高质量工作

  • hit your targets 达成目标

  • the number one thing 首要因素

  • get your point across to your team 把观点清晰传达给团队

  • creates friction 产生摩擦

  • removes that barrier 消除这一障碍

  • straight away 立刻，马上

What benefits can working in a foreign country bring to people's career development?

I'd say the most obvious benefit is monetary. People generally get paid better when they take a role abroad, that's just the reality of it for a lot of industries.

But the other big one, and the more valuable one long term I think, is adaptability. Like I said before, you kind of have to re-learn so many things when you work in a different country, and that ability to adjust and pick up new ways of working and thinking is priceless. It's the kind of skill that stays with you and makes you much more employable further down the road.

  • the reality of it 现实

  • valuable 有价值的

  • priceless 极其珍贵；无价

  • further down the road 在未来；日后

item.title: 雅思口语Part 1高分语料 | Typing 你喜欢打字还是手写？
item.description:
你好呀，欢迎收听：英语考试Cat 🐱🐱🐱🐱

Do you type on a desktop or laptop keyboard every day?

Yeah, sure, not a day goes by without using a computer. I use a desktop keyboard for work, my laptop keyboard at home, and I also type on my smartphone daily. As for the desktop keyboard, it actually took me some time to get accustomed to it, but y'know, just like with many other skills, practice makes perfect.

  • not a day goes by without 没有一天不

  • using a computer 使用电脑

  • type on 在…… 上打字

  • took me some time to 花了一些时间去

  • get accustomed to 习惯于

  • just like with 就像

  • practice makes perfect 熟能生巧

When did you learn how to type on a keyboard?

I first picked up Chinese typing during computer classes in junior high school. Then I got the hang of typing in English when I was at college after I got my very first laptop. I wasn't particularly fast on it to begin with, but my typing speed gradually improved with practice.

  • picked up 学会

  • junior high school 初中

  • got the hang of 掌握…… 的窍门

  • got my very first 得到我的第一个

  • improved with practice 在练习中提升

How do you improve your typing?

Well, it's pretty straightforward. Constant practice is how I got better — besides taking a typing class what else can you do besides practice really? Keyboard formats are largely similar on any device; basically, it's size that's the main difference. So once you become confident typing on one device, you tend to adapt naturally to the others.

  • straightforward 简单直接的

  • formats 格式

  • device 设备

  • become confident 变得熟练、有信心

  • adapt naturally 自然适应

Do you prefer typing or handwriting?

It actually depends. Typing is undeniably far more convenient, but I still love that tangible feeling of putting pen to paper. As a matter of fact, I keep a notebook at work to jot down sudden thoughts along with updating my to‑do list. And at home, I always keep a pile of paper right next to my laptop. There's just something about writing by hand that helps me memorise information better.

  • undeniably 无可否认

  • convenient 方便

  • tangible 实实在在

  • jot down 快速记下

  • thoughts 想法

  • updating 更新

  • to-do list 待办清单

  • a pile of paper 一叠纸

  • writing by hand 手写

item.title: 雅思口语Part 1高分语料 | Dreams 还记得自己做过的梦吗？
item.description:
你好呀，欢迎收听：英语考试Cat 🐱🐱🐱🐱

Can you remember the dreams you had?

Not really. More often than not, I completely forget my dreams by the following morning, assuming I even dreamt at all. That said, on the rare occasions I do hold onto fragments of a dream, I tend to tell my close friends about it the next day, particularly if it happens to be a nightmare.

  • More often than not 通常

  • on the rare occasions 在极少数情况下

  • fragments of 片段

  • close friends 挚友

  • if it happens to be 如果碰巧是

Do you share your dreams with others?

Yes. As I just mentioned, if I can recall what I dreamt about overnight, I'll bring it up with my closest friends the next day, and then we'll talk about what those dreams might signify. For example, a nightmare could reflect mental stress. What's more, if I dream about certain family members, I will also mention it to my relatives during our phone calls.

  • recall 回忆起

  • bring it up 提起这件事

  • signify 意味着

  • mental stress 精神压力

  • mention it to 和…… 说起这件事

Do you think dreams have special meanings?

I believe they do, yes. I feel the dreams we experience at night are closely linked to our subconscious. To give you an example, if I'm in high spirits before going to sleep, I may end up having a pleasant, light‑hearted dream. Conversely, if I've been feeling under a lot of pressure, I might get nightmares.

  • closely linked to 和…… 紧密相关

  • subconscious 潜意识

  • in high spirits 心情愉悦

  • end up having 最终会

  • light-hearted 轻松愉快

  • under a lot of pressure 承受很大压力

Do you want to make your dreams come true?

Well, one of my aspirations is to become fluent in Spanish, and naturally I would love to turn that into reality. Having said that, I'm aware I'm no longer putting in any real effort to work towards this goal, so realistically, it will probably never materialize. But I do have other dreams, and I think some of them will come true, but I can't ay what they are as that might jinx them!

  • turn that into reality 将其变为现实

  • no longer putting in any real effort 不再付出实际的努力

  • materialize 实现

  • jinx 倒霉，破坏（好运）

item.title: 雅思口语Part 2高分语料 | 描述一种你在特殊场合会吃的食物
item.description:
你好呀，欢迎收听：英语考试Cat 🐱🐱🐱🐱

Describe a kind of food you eat on a special occasion

You should say:

• What the occasion is

• What the food is

• How it is made or where it comes from

• Why it is special to you

 

I'd like to talk about a special food that my family always has for the Spring Festival, our most important traditional holiday.

This specialty is smoked spicy pork sausages. It's a really well‑known local delicacy from my home province, Sichuan.

Making these sausages is quite a process. We use pork that's roughly ninety percent lean and ten percent fat. When I was little, adults would mince the meat by hand, mincing by machine was unheard of. Then we mix into the mince whopping amounts of different spices. Almost everyone from where I come from goes for that classic spicy‑numbing chili flavor. Next, we stuff the seasoned meat into cleaned pork intestines. Subsequently, the sausages are smoked continuously for around half a month. To prepare them for serving, we boil them in water. Once they are cooked through, let cool, and slice-up the sausage fairly thinly., and it's great just by itself or even as an ingredient in any dish that calls for sausage.

For me, these smoked sausages are more than just tasty food. Preparing them is a big winter tradition in rural parts of Sichuan. Every household gets busy making sausages ahead of Spring Festival. The air is thick with the aroma of smoked pork, and when I was a child, it was hard not to salivate waiting to eat them around the table. It's one of the most fun childhood memories for me. And even now, I have them at home in the freezer.

  • local delicacy 当地特色美食

  • quite a process 工序相当繁琐

  • lean 瘦肉

  • mince 剁碎；肉末

  • unheard of 闻所未闻

  • whopping amounts 大量

  • goes for 偏爱

  • chili flavor 辣椒风味

item.description:

You should say:

and explain why you like this book or film.

I'd like to talk about an animated film that's full of animal characters, and its name is Zootopia.

There's a huge variety of creatures featured in this movie, covering both predators and prey. To start with, the two lead roles are Judy, a young rabbit, and her loyal best friend Nick, a witty fox. Her boss at the police station is an ox, and there's plenty of other species throughout the movie: elephants, famously slow sloths, polar bears, and a graceful gazelle, just to name a few.

The movie is about Judy, a small-town rabbit whose lifelong dream is to become a police officer in the big city of Zootopia. Back in her town, everyone around her laughs at her dream, since rabbits have never worked as cops before. But she refuses to give up, passes all the tough training, and finally lands a police post. Later, she stumbles upon a mysterious missing-animal case and teams up with the witty fox, Nick, to solve it. Together they uncover a conspiracy that creates conflict between predators and prey, and in the end, they fix the division and bring peace back to Zootopia.

The main reason I enjoyed this film is how relatable Judy's journey feels to me. She doesn't come from a privileged background; no one in her family has connections to give her an easy shortcut. Yet she never lets other people's prejudice or self-doubt stop her from pursuing what she dreams to do, and of course, admirably, for doing what she thinks is right.

item.title: 雅思口语Part 2高分语料 | 描述一件花费超出预期的物品
item.description:
你好呀，欢迎收听：英语考试Cat 🐱🐱🐱🐱

Describe something you bought that cost more than you expected

You should say:

•    What the item was

•    When and where you bought it

•    Why it cost more than you had expected

•    And explain how you felt about spending that much money and whether you think it was worth it

 

I'd like to talk about a takeaway pizza I bought that ended up costing way more than I'd planned for when I was in the US.

First off, the item itself was just a regular to-go pizza. The menu listed the pie at 29 US dollars. But then the restaurant automatically added a mandatory 20 percent tip, which worked out to 5.8 dollars. Altogether, I paid 34.8 dollars for the pizza.

It happened when I was in downtown Charleston, and that was back in April this year. I was walking in the city center that morning looking for lunch, so I popped into a local pizzeria.

I knew downtown Charleston is a pricey east-coast US city, so I braced myself for slightly higher food prices. Even so, I was caught off guard by just how overpriced it was. The pizza was small for its nearly 30-dollar pricetag. What annoyed me most though, was the compulsory service charge. This was takeaway. Anyway, I placed my order at the cashier, left, and returned half an hour later to bring it to my car. There was no table service, no server checking on me, nothing that justified a 20 percent tip. That surcharge felt like a rip-off.

To make matters worse, I’d parked my car in a parking lot a few blocks away while waiting for the food, and parking set me back another 12 dollars on top of everything else.

By the time I added up every expense, the whole experience blew my original budget out of the water. I definitely do not think it was worth the total cost. The food tasted fine, but the unnecessary takeaway tipping fee and expensive parking piled up into a ridiculous bill.

I'd like to talk about a little gift I bestowed upon my closest friend just last week.

It's a tiny ocean-blue car model, sleek and detailed, and I picked that specific shade of blue  for a really meaningful reason.

I gave this present to my best friend, who has just finished his master's degree and is officially graduating this month. Blue's always been his favorite color, so choosing this colour was a no-brainer when I was shopping for something to celebrate his big milestone.

The main reason I settled on a miniature car stems from all the good times we've had together. He's obsessed with driving. Whenever he travels overseas, he'll always rent a car and head off on week-long road trips to explore new places. Back in the day, he actually owned his own car, but he sold it a few years ago.

Now, whenever he feels like going for a drive, he still rents a car—and when I was in Singapore, he almost always invited me to tag along. We explored some hidden gems of Singapore and those drives were some of my best memories from studying in Singapore.

This is exactly why this little car model struck me as the ideal gift. It wasn't costly, but when I handed it to him, he told me he loved it and that it brought back childhood memories. Hearing that made me genuinely glad, knowing I had picked a present that brought joy to my best friend.

item.title: 雅思口语Part 2高分语料 | 描述一场你现场观看的体育赛事
item.description:

Describe a sports match you watched live (not on TV).

You should say:

  • When it happened

  • What you watched

Two years ago in June, I headed to a huge stadium in Texas to watch a professional league baseball game. From what I recall, it was Kansas versus Texas, and the venue was absolutely packed with thousands of hyped-up supporters. The whole atmosphere was electric—every single person around me was roaring and cheering their hearts out for the Texas team. Giant digital screens hung all around the stands too, constantly playing clips to rev-up the spectators and egg us on to shout even louder.

I barely knew the ins and outs of baseball back then. Luckily, my friend, who's a huge baseball fan, walked me through the basic rules as the match unfolded, so I sort of had a play-by-play explanation of what was going on.

This was my very first time ever watching a sports game live in a stadium, so the whole experience was eye-opening to say the least. And it wasn't just the game itself that stuck with me. Between innings, there were upbeat cheerleading routines performed, lighthearted and funny adverts played across those massive screens, and stalls selling all kinds of tasty snacks and cold drinks. I grabbed a few treats, like a hotdog and slushy, and took them back to my seat and then ate and drank while the next half of the game played on. It really was an incredible time.

Overall, it's one of the best experiences I've ever had. I got to soak up that raw, buzzing energy that only live sporting events can deliver—something you'd never get from simply watching on television.

Most Chinese students spend many years studying English. They memorize thousands of words, learn complicated grammar rules, complete endless reading comprehension exercises, and often achieve excellent results in their school examinations.

Yet many of these same students are surprised, even shocked, when they take the IELTS examination for the first time. Some receive a score of 5.5 when they expected a 7.

The simple truth is this:

Absolutely, I'm such an easy laugh actually, even silly one-liners can crack me up instantly.
